hard_think: The query-entry workspace and verification authority are distinct evidence roles even when they belong to the same Git repository and commit.
Recycling the authority as the workspace makes independent configured-authority selection self-referential; the correct resolver rejection must remain intact.
Passing an explicit internal workspace root is smaller and safer than environment mutation, fallback, a preselected-authority API, or repeated maintenance.
Candidate tests and a production-shaped CURRENT proof do not replace the first merged exact-main controller replay.
dialectic_sweep: Weakening authority-equals-workspace validation would make the failed controller appear green but collapse the independent clean-authority boundary.
Letting query_once accept a preselected authority would avoid selection repetition but create a privileged bypass surface without a demonstrated need.
Clearing the authority environment is compact but process-global and race-prone; explicit data flow preserves concurrency and provenance.
Repeating maintenance could hide the false negative but add external effects after a transaction that already succeeded.
first_principles: A read begins at the caller workspace, independently selects current clean authority, and accepts only evidence bound to that selection.
The prompt supplies query content only; controller roots remain internal trusted inputs.
Every production caller must preserve the same root separation and every malformed topology must fail closed.
This slice repairs controller truth only; exact runtime closure, A-grade, retrieval-quality RSI, and merged live acceptance remain separate gates.
